architect.additional.form.arrayFields.op.defaultMessage: No options have been added yet.
architect.additional.form.arrayFields.op.description: Message shown in place of the list when a categorical or ordinal variable has no options yet.

architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.i.defaultMessage: If you believe you are seeing this message in error, please help us to troubleshoot this issue by creating a topic on our <ExternalLink> community website </ExternalLink> with further details.
architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.i.description: Paragraph in the error dialog shown when an imported data file is invalid. ExternalLink wraps the words that link to the Network Canvas community forum, where the researcher can report a problem.

architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.p.defaultMessage: Please see our <ExternalLink> documentation page </ExternalLink> on using external data by clicking the button below.
architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.p.description: Paragraph in the error dialog shown when an imported data file is invalid. ExternalLink wraps the words that link to the documentation page about using external data (CSV or JSON resources).

architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.t.defaultMessage: The file you attempted to import contained invalid attribute names.
architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.t.description: First paragraph of the error dialog when an imported data file has column headings that are not valid variable names. A more specific message follows it.

architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.t.defaultMessage: The file you attempted to import is not in a format supported by Interviewer.
architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.t.description: First paragraph of the error dialog when an imported file cannot be read as a supported resource. Interviewer is the Network Canvas interview app. A more specific message follows it.

architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.t.defaultMessage: The file you attempted to import contained data with a different number of columns to the header row.
architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.t.description: First paragraph of the error dialog when an imported CSV data file has rows with a different number of columns than the heading row. A more specific message follows it.

architect.additional.form.autoFileDrop.v.description: Button-styled link in the error dialog for an invalid imported data file; opens the documentation page about supported resource types.

architect.additional.form.fields.variabl.defaultMessage: To create your first attribute of this type, type a name above and press enter. See our <ExternalLink> {value1} </ExternalLink> for more information.
architect.additional.form.fields.variabl.description: Hint in the variable search window, shown when no variable exists yet for this node type or edge type. ExternalLink wraps value1, which is a link to the documentation on naming. Attribute means codebook variable.

architect.additional.home.libraryPanel.b.defaultMessage: Because your work is stored locally, clearing Architect's app data, or using "Clear all protocols", will permanently remove it. Download the protocol as a .netcanvas file to save a copy or move it to another device. See our guide to saving and backing up your work for more.
architect.additional.home.libraryPanel.b.description: Paragraph in the Protocol Storage dialog warning that protocols saved in the browser are lost if app data is cleared or Clear all protocols is used. code wraps the file extension .netcanvas; ExternalLink wraps the link to the saving and backing up guide.

architect.additional.home.libraryPanel.l.defaultMessage: Looking for inspiration? Browse example research protocols in the <ExternalLink>Protocol Gallery</ExternalLink>.
architect.additional.home.libraryPanel.l.description: Paragraph in the Protocol Storage dialog suggesting example protocols. ExternalLink wraps the words Protocol Gallery, which link to the online gallery.

architect.additional.home.libraryPanel.m.defaultMessage: More examples of Network Canvas protocols can be found on our <ExternalLink>Protocol Gallery</ExternalLink>.
architect.additional.home.libraryPanel.m.description: Text of the Looking for more card on the start screen. ExternalLink wraps the words Protocol Gallery, which link to the online gallery of example protocols.

architect.additional.newVariableWindow.n.description: Label of the button that adds one more option to the list of allowed values, in the window for creating a new codebook variable (called an attribute here).

architect.additional.pages.assetsPage.im.defaultMessage: Import external data resources to use in your protocol — images, video, audio, or network data. See our <ExternalLink> documentation </ExternalLink> for more information.
architect.additional.pages.assetsPage.im.description: Introductory text under the heading of the Resource Library page. The <ExternalLink> tag wraps the words that link to the documentation about resources (uploaded files).

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: If the problem persists, reach out on our <ExternalLink> community website. </ExternalLink>
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: Small print at the bottom of an error dialog shown when opening a protocol fails. The <ExternalLink> tag wraps the words that link to the Network Canvas community website.

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: In order to open it, you will need to install a version of Architect that supports schema version {value1}.
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: Second paragraph of the error dialog for a protocol made for a newer schema. value1 is the schema version number of the protocol; it is the version of the protocol file format, not of the app.
Heading above the list of changes for one schema version, in the dialog shown to researchers when Architect offers to upgrade an older protocol. {version} is the schema version number.
Button that dismisses an error or warning dialog shown when opening a protocol.

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: Please see our <ExternalLink> documentation on protocol schemas </ExternalLink> to locate an appropriate version, and for further information on this topic.
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: Last paragraph of the error dialog for a protocol made for a newer schema. The <ExternalLink> tag wraps the words that link to the documentation on protocol schemas.

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: Protocol not compatible with current version
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: Title of the error dialog shown when the protocol being opened was made for a newer schema than this version of Architect supports.
Accessible name of the list of protocol validation errors; read only by screen readers.
Title of the error dialog shown when a protocol file could not be opened because it failed validation against the protocol schema.

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: This protocol refers to files that were not included in it: {assetList}. Everything else opened normally. Add the files again in Resources — until you do, the protocol cannot be downloaded.
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: Body of the warning dialog shown when a protocol opened without some resource files it refers to. assetList is the list of missing file names. Resources is the name of the page where files are added again; the protocol cannot be downloaded until they are.
Title of the warning dialog shown after a protocol opens but some of the resource files (images, video, audio, network data) it refers to were not included in the protocol file.

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: The protocol could not be opened due to validation errors:
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: Introductory sentence in the validation error dialog, shown above the technical details of the validation errors found in the protocol file.

architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.defaultMessage: This protocol is not compatible with the current version of Architect.
architect.additional.protocolOpenDialogs.description: First paragraph of the error dialog shown when the protocol being opened needs a newer version of Architect than this one.
Title of the dialog shown when the researcher opens a protocol made for an older schema and the only option is to upgrade a copy of it to the current schema.

architect.additional.typeEditor.shapeVar.description: Button below the list of thresholds in the node type editor's shape mapping. Adds a threshold: a number at or above which nodes are drawn with a chosen shape.

architect.additional.typeEditor.shapeVar.defaultMessage: No thresholds yet — every value uses the default shape.
architect.additional.typeEditor.shapeVar.description: Empty-state message in the thresholds list of the node type editor's shape mapping, shown before any threshold is added.

architect.app.storageFailure.defaultMessage: Your recent changes could not be saved to this device, which can happen if local storage is full or unavailable. To avoid losing work, download a copy of your protocol.
architect.app.storageFailure.description: Body of the error dialog shown when autosave fails because browser storage on this device is full or unavailable. Advises the researcher to download a copy of the protocol file.

architect.appUpdate.appUpdatePill.v.description: Label of the pill in the Architect header showing the installed app version. appVersion is the version number, for example 9.0.1; the leading v stands for version.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.addA.defaultMessage: Add a new resource to this protocol.
architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.addA.description: Hint under the Import resource section heading, saying that a new resource (an uploaded file or API key) can be added to the protocol here.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.areY.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete this resource? You can restore it with Undo while this protocol remains open.
architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.areY.description: Body of the confirmation dialog for deleting a resource. Reassures the researcher that Undo can restore the resource while the protocol stays open.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.brow.defaultMessage: Browse and manage resources stored in this protocol.
architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.brow.description: Hint under the Resource library section heading, saying that the researcher can browse, preview, download and delete the resources stored in the protocol.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.cann.description: Title of the dialog shown when the researcher tries to delete an uploaded resource (file) that a stage in the protocol still uses.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.cann.defaultMessage: Cannot delete this resource because it is used within your interview. Remove any uses of the resource, and try again.
architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.cann.description: Body of the dialog explaining that a resource used by a stage cannot be deleted until its uses are removed. Also the fallback message when adding the missing file for a resource fails without a specific error.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.choo.defaultMessage: Choose the missing file for this resource
architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.choo.description: Accessible name of the hidden file picker that opens when the researcher supplies a file for a resource whose file is missing from the protocol; read only by screen readers.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.coul.description: Title of the error dialog shown when the file the researcher chose to replace a missing resource file could not be added.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.dele.description: Title of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm deleting an uploaded resource (file) from the protocol.
Label of the destructive button that confirms deleting a resource, in the delete confirmation dialog.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.impo.description: Heading of the section of the resource library where the researcher uploads a new resource (image, video, audio, network data, GeoJSON or API key).

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.oK.description: Button that dismisses an informational or error dialog in the resource library.

architect.assetBrowser.assetBrowser.reso.description: Heading of the section listing all resources (uploaded files and API keys) stored in the protocol.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.delete.description: Accessible name of the icon button on a resource card that deletes the resource; read only by screen readers. name is the resource name.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.deleteR.description: Tooltip of the icon button on a resource card that deletes the resource. Delete here is a verb.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.downloa.description: Accessible name of the icon button on a resource card that downloads the resource file; read only by screen readers. name is the resource name.
Tooltip of the icon button on a resource card that downloads the resource file. Download here is a verb.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.isInUse.defaultMessage: {name} is in use and cannot be deleted
architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.isInUse.description: Accessible name of the delete button on a resource card when a stage still uses the resource, so it cannot be deleted; read only by screen readers. name is the resource name.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.missing.description: Badge on a resource card showing that the protocol lists this resource but its file is not stored, because the imported protocol file did not contain it.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.preview.description: Accessible name of the icon button on a resource card that opens a preview of the resource; read only by screen readers. name is the resource name.
Tooltip of the icon button on a resource card that opens a preview of the resource. Preview here is a verb.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.replace.description: Accessible name of the icon button on a resource card that lets the researcher choose the missing file for the resource; read only by screen readers. name is the resource name.
Tooltip of the icon button on a resource card that opens a file picker so the researcher can supply the file missing for this resource.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.thisRes.defaultMessage: This resource is in use by the protocol and cannot be deleted
architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.thisRes.description: Tooltip of the delete button on a resource card when the resource is used by a stage in the protocol and therefore cannot be deleted.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.unused.description: Badge on a resource card showing that no stage in the protocol uses this resource.

architect.assetBrowser.assetCard.videoPr.description: Accessible name of the video thumbnail on a resource card; read only by screen readers. name is the researcher-given name of the video resource.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.aPI.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows only API key resources (for example a map service key).

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.all.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows resources of every kind.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.aud.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows only audio resources. Names the kind of file.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.geo.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows only GeoJSON map data resources. GeoJSON is a file format name.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.ima.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows only image resources. Names the kind of file.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.net.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows only network data resources (a file of nodes or edges, such as CSV or JSON). Names the kind of file.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.config.vid.description: Option in the filter switcher above the resource library that shows only video resources. Names the kind of file.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.filterReso.description: Accessible name of the switcher above the resource library that filters resources by kind; read only by screen readers.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.noResource.description: Message shown in place of the resource cards when no resources match the selected filter or the protocol has none.

architect.assetBrowser.assets.resourceLi.description: Accessible name of the grid of resource cards in the resource library; read only by screen readers.

architect.assetBrowser.duplicateRowsWarn.description: Button that dismisses the duplicate-rows warning dialog.

architect.assetBrowser.preview.closePrev.description: Button in the footer of the resource preview dialog that closes the dialog.

architect.assetBrowser.preview.copyAPIKe.description: Button in the footer of the preview dialog for an API key resource that copies the key to the clipboard. Replaces the download button for API keys.

architect.assetBrowser.preview.downloadA.description: Button in the footer of the resource preview dialog that downloads the previewed resource file (image, video, audio, network data or GeoJSON). Download is a verb; asset means resource.

architect.assetBrowser.preview.unavailab.description: Message shown in the resource preview dialog when the resource has a kind that cannot be previewed.

architect.assetBrowser.unusedAssetsAlert.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {This resource is not used by any stage in your protocol and is marked Unused below. Reference it in a stage, or remove it to keep your protocol tidy.} other {These resources are not used by any stage in your protocol and are marked Unused below. Reference them in a stage, or remove them to keep your protocol tidy.}}
architect.assetBrowser.unusedAssetsAlert.description: Body of the warning at the top of the resource library about resources that no stage uses. count is the number of unused resources; strong marks the word Unused, which matches the Unused badge shown on each such resource card.

architect.assetBrowser.unusedAssetsAlert.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# unused resource} other {# unused resources}}
architect.assetBrowser.unusedAssetsAlert.description: Title of the warning at the top of the resource library when some resources are not used by any stage. count is the number of unused resources (uploaded files or API keys).

architect.assetBrowser.useExternalDataDo.description: Body of the error dialog shown when a resource download fails. value1 is the name of the resource; it appears in quotation marks.
Title of the error dialog shown when downloading a resource file from the resource library fails.
Button that dismisses the download-failed error dialog.

architect.assetMetadata.apikey.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assetMetadata.audio.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assetMetadata.geojson.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assetMetadata.image.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assetMetadata.interviewNetwork.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assetMetadata.network.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assetMetadata.video.description: Researcher-facing resource metadata label; resource names and stable file/type identifiers are kept unchanged.

architect.assets.geoJSON.showingOfFeatur.description: Note above the table in the GeoJSON resource preview, shown when the file has more features (map shapes or points) than the table displays. ROW_LIMIT is the number of features shown; value2 is the total number of features in the file.

architect.assets.network.showingOfRows.description: Note above the table in the network data resource preview, shown when the file has more rows (nodes) than the table displays. ROW_LIMIT is the number of rows shown; value2 is the total number of rows in the file.

architect.assets.table.toggleSortBy.description: Tooltip on a column header of the data table in a resource preview. Clicking the header cycles the table between ascending, descending and unsorted order by that column.

architect.brand.returnToStartScreen.description: Accessible name of the Architect logo button in the app header; read only by screen readers. Activating it closes the current protocol and returns to the start screen.

architect.builtInWording.missingInDefaul.defaultMessage: Network Canvas has no built-in wording, such as button labels and messages, in {language}. Translate it into {language}, or make a language that has built-in wording the default. The protocol can’t be downloaded until then.
architect.builtInWording.missingInDefaul.description: Shown while the protocol’s default language is one Network Canvas has no built-in wording in (for example Mexican Spanish or Japanese), so the wording Network Canvas supplies (button labels, messages and similar) has no text in it. The researcher can translate that wording into the language in the translation table, or make another of the protocol’s languages that Network Canvas has wording in (for example Spanish) the default. language is the name of the default language, for example “Spanish (Mexico)”.

architect.builtInWording.showMissing.description: Link in the notice about built-in wording missing in the protocol’s default language. It opens the translation table showing only the text that has no translation in that language.

architect.chrome.codebook.controlsColumn.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the button in a row of the codebook variables table that deletes the variable (attribute). Delete is a verb.
Tooltip and accessible name of the disabled delete button in a row of the codebook variables table, shown when a stage uses the variable so it cannot be deleted.

architect.chrome.codebook.entityTypeDial.description: Title of the dialog for creating a new node type or edge type. entityLabel is the word Node or Edge.
The word Edge, inserted as entityLabel into the title of the dialog for creating or editing an edge type (a kind of relationship between nodes).
Title of the dialog for editing an existing node type or edge type. entityLabel is the word Node or Edge.
The word Node, inserted as entityLabel into the title of the dialog for creating or editing a node type (a kind of person or thing participants name).

architect.chrome.home.libraryPanel.anExa.defaultMessage: An example introducing the key features and techniques available in Network Canvas.
architect.chrome.home.libraryPanel.anExa.description: Description of the Sample Protocol in the Templates tab of the start screen; used only if the sample protocol has no description of its own.

architect.chrome.home.libraryPanel.thisP.description: Shown in the protocol info dialog in place of the description when the protocol has none.

architect.chrome.home.libraryPanel.yourP.defaultMessage: {protocolCount, plural, one {Your protocol is saved only on this device. It is never uploaded to a server.} other {Your # protocols are saved only on this device. They are never uploaded to a server.}}
architect.chrome.home.libraryPanel.yourP.description: Tooltip on the info button above the Recent list of the start screen, reassuring the researcher that protocols stay on this device. protocolCount is the number of saved protocols.

architect.chrome.projectNav.projectActio.description: Label of the toolbar button, shown on the Resources, Codebook, Languages and Summary pages, that goes back to the Stages page showing the stage timeline.
Label of the toolbar button, shown on the Stages page, that closes the protocol and goes back to the start screen listing protocols.

architect.chrome.projectNav.projectNav.u.description: Name shown in the top bar breadcrumb when the open protocol has no name yet.

architect.chrome.projectNav.stageEditorN.description: Name shown in the top bar breadcrumb of the stage editor when the open protocol has no name yet.

architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.theO.defaultMessage: The other tab has been closed, but an editor is still open here. Nothing can be saved or loaded in this tab until you finish or cancel that editor.
architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.theO.description: Text of the banner across the protocol editor. The other browser tab that held this protocol has closed, but an editor (such as a dialog opened from a stage) is still open in this tab and must be finished or cancelled before anything can be saved.

architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.theO.defaultMessage: The other tab has been closed, but your unsaved changes to this stage cannot be combined with the version it saved. Nothing can be saved here until you decide which to keep.
architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.theO.description: Text of the banner across the protocol editor. The other browser tab has closed, but the researcher's unsaved changes to the open stage cannot be combined with what that tab saved. The researcher must choose which version to keep.

architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.this.defaultMessage: This protocol has been opened in another tab, which now holds the saved copy. Nothing you change here can be saved, including any unsaved changes in the editor you have open. Close the other tab to carry on editing here, or close that editor to keep looking through the protocol read-only.
architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.this.description: Text of the warning banner when the protocol was opened in another browser tab while an editor (such as a dialog opened from a stage) was open in this tab. Changes made here cannot be saved.

architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.this.defaultMessage: This protocol has been opened in another tab, which now holds the saved copy. Nothing you change here can be saved, including any unsaved changes to this stage. Close the other tab to carry on editing here, or discard your changes to keep looking through the protocol read-only.
architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.this.description: Text of the warning banner when the protocol was opened in another browser tab while a stage editor was open in this tab. Changes to the stage cannot be saved; the Discard Changes button leaves the editor.

architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.this.defaultMessage: This protocol is open in another tab, which holds the saved copy, so it is read-only here. You can look through every page, but nothing can be changed. Close the other tab to edit it in this one.
architect.chrome.protocolLockBanner.this.description: Text of the informational banner across the protocol editor when another browser tab holds the saved copy of the protocol. This tab can only be browsed, not edited, until the other tab is closed.

architect.chrome.protocolRouteGuard.edit.defaultMessage: The other tab is no longer editing this protocol, so you can edit it here again.
architect.chrome.protocolRouteGuard.edit.description: Screen-reader announcement made when a tab that was showing a protocol read-only, because another tab was editing it, becomes able to edit it.

architect.chrome.protocolSummary.assetBa.description: Shown in the printable protocol summary in place of a resource's details when a stage refers to an uploaded resource that is missing from the protocol. id is the missing resource's identifier.

architect.chrome.protocolSummary.stage.m.description: Initial map center in latitude, longitude order. Values are locale-formatted signed decimal degrees with four decimal places; use unambiguous punctuation for the locale.

architect.chrome.protocolSummary.stage.q.description: Value of the type row in the quick add table of the printable protocol summary when the variable's data type cannot be found.

architect.chrome.stageEditor.stageEditor.description: Label of the Preview button in the stage editor toolbar while the preview window is being opened. Replaces the label Preview for a moment.
Label of the button in the stage editor toolbar that opens the interview preview in a new window, starting at the stage being edited. The verb, not the name of the window.

architect.chrome.timeline.timelineStageR.description: Accessible name of the control on a timeline stage that opens the stage for editing; read only by screen readers. position is its number in the timeline, stageName its title, interfaceName the name of its interface type.
Accessible name of the control on a timeline stage that opens the stage for editing, used when the stage type has no known name. position is its number in the timeline; stageName is its title.
Accessible name of the control that opens a stage on the timeline while this tab can only view the protocol, because another tab is editing it.
Accessible name of the control that opens a stage on the timeline while this tab can only view the protocol, because another tab is editing it. Used when the stage type has no known name.

architect.codebook.codebook.createEdgeTy.description: Button beside the Edge Types heading on the Codebook page that opens a dialog for creating a new edge type. Create is a verb.

architect.codebook.codebook.createNodeTy.description: Button beside the Node Types heading on the Codebook page that opens a dialog for creating a new node type. Create is a verb.

architect.codebook.codebook.edgeTypes.description: Codebook section heading. value1 is the total number of edge types in the protocol. An edge type is a kind of relationship between two nodes, such as Friend.

architect.codebook.codebook.ego.description: Heading of the Codebook page section for the ego, the study participant being interviewed, whose own attributes (variables) are listed under it.

architect.codebook.codebook.egoAttribute.description: Title of the section on the Codebook page listing the ego attributes, the codebook variables recorded about the participant themselves rather than about people they name.

architect.codebook.codebook.networkAsset.description: Codebook section heading. value1 is the total number of network resources in the protocol. A network resource is an uploaded file of nodes or edges that stages can use as a roster.

architect.codebook.codebook.noEdgeTypesY.description: Message under the Edge Types heading on the Codebook page when the protocol has no edge types.

architect.codebook.codebook.noNodeTypesY.description: Message under the Node Types heading on the Codebook page when the protocol has no node types.

architect.codebook.codebook.nodeTypes.description: Codebook section heading. value1 is the total number of node types in the protocol. A node type is a kind of person or thing that participants name, such as Person.

architect.codebook.codebook.reviewTheAtt.defaultMessage: Review the attributes collected about the participant.
architect.codebook.codebook.reviewTheAtt.description: Hint under the Ego attributes section title, saying that the section lists the attributes (variables) collected about the participant.

architect.codebook.codebook.searchTheCod.description: Label of the search field at the top of the Codebook page, which filters the node types, edge types and variables listed below it by name.

architect.codebook.codebook.searchTypesA.defaultMessage: Search types and attributes by name...
architect.codebook.codebook.searchTypesA.description: Placeholder inside the search field at the top of the Codebook page. Types means node types and edge types; attributes means the codebook variables recorded about them.

architect.codebook.codebook.showUnusedOn.description: Label of the checkbox at the top of the Codebook page that, when ticked, lists only variables that no stage uses.

architect.codebook.codebook.thereAreCurr.defaultMessage: There are currently no types or attributes defined in this protocol. Use the buttons below to create your first node or edge type, or add ego attributes.
architect.codebook.codebook.thereAreCurr.description: Message on the Codebook page when the protocol has no node types, edge types, ego attributes or network resources yet. The buttons below it create a node type, an edge type or an ego attribute.

architect.codebook.egoType.addAttribute.description: Button in the Ego attributes section of the Codebook page that opens a window for adding a new variable (attribute) recorded about the participant.

architect.codebook.egoType.noEgoAttribut.defaultMessage: No ego attributes match the current filter.
architect.codebook.egoType.noEgoAttribut.description: Message in the Ego attributes section of the Codebook page when ego attributes exist but none match the current search text or the Show unused only checkbox.
Message in the Ego attributes section of the Codebook page when no ego attributes (variables about the participant) have been defined.

architect.codebook.entity.ego.description: The interviewee entity heading in the researcher codebook, not a persisted entity identifier.

architect.codebook.entityType.addAttribu.description: Button on a node type or edge type section of the Codebook page that opens a window for adding a new variable (attribute) recorded for that type.

architect.codebook.entityType.areYouSure.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete the {entity, select, node {node} edge {edge} other {ego}} type “{name}”? You can restore it with Undo while this protocol remains open.
architect.codebook.entityType.areYouSure.description: Body of the confirmation dialog for deleting a node type or edge type. entity is node, edge or ego, selecting the word before type; name is the type name, shown in quotation marks. Notes that Undo can restore it while the protocol stays open.

architect.codebook.entityType.cannotDele.description: Title of the dialog shown when the researcher tries to delete a node type or edge type that stages still use.

architect.codebook.entityType.deleteEnti.description: Label and tooltip of the button on a node type or edge type section of the Codebook page that deletes the type. Delete is a verb; entity means the node type or edge type.

architect.codebook.entityType.deleteType.description: Title of the dialog, and label of its destructive confirm button, for deleting a node type or edge type from the codebook. Delete is a verb.

architect.codebook.entityType.editEntity.description: Button on a node type or edge type section of the Codebook page that opens the dialog for editing the type. Edit is a verb; entity means the node type or edge type.

architect.codebook.entityType.inUseInSta.defaultMessage: {value1, plural, one {In use in # stage — remove usages first} other {In use in # stages — remove usages first}}
architect.codebook.entityType.inUseInSta.description: Tooltip on the disabled Delete button of a node type or edge type that stages use. value1 is the number of stages using the type; the researcher must remove those uses before deleting.

architect.codebook.entityType.notInUse.description: Warning badge on a node type or edge type section of the Codebook page, shown when no stage uses the type.

architect.codebook.entityType.oK.description: Button that dismisses the cannot-delete-type dialog.

architect.importSize.compressed.description: Import refusal before a protocol archive is buffered. Sizes are rounded mebibytes, shown consistently with the existing MB convention.

architect.importSize.expanded.defaultMessage: This protocol file expands to more data than can be opened safely ({size, number} MB). It may be corrupt. The maximum supported size is {maximum, number} MB.
architect.importSize.expanded.description: Import refusal before media inflation when the archive declares an excessive expanded size.

architect.installBanner.installArchitect.description: Accessible name of the banner warning that stored protocols could be deleted by the browser unless Architect is installed; read only by screen readers.

architect.interface.capability.createEdg.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.createNod.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.edgeAttri.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.egoData.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.nodeAttri.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.provideIn.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.rosterDat.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.showMedia.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card; the value remains a stable internal key.

architect.interface.capability.utilities.description: Capability filter and badge on an interface card, for stages that set up the interview (such as choosing its language or setting a passphrase) rather than collect or display network data.

architect.interface.description.AlterEdg.defaultMessage: An edge interpreter interface that captures attribute data via a form.
architect.interface.description.AlterEdg.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.AlterFor.defaultMessage: An interface that allows the participant to fill out a form for each alter in the interview network.
architect.interface.description.AlterFor.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Anonymis.defaultMessage: An interface that allows the participant to set a passphrase for node anonymisation.
architect.interface.description.Anonymis.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Categori.defaultMessage: A name interpreter interface that collects nominal data by allowing the participant to drag and drop alters into circles representing a category.
architect.interface.description.Categori.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.DyadCens.defaultMessage: A name interpreter interface that creates edges by systematically surveying all alters in the interview network.
architect.interface.description.DyadCens.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.EgoForm.defaultMessage: An interface that collects data on your participant (ego).
architect.interface.description.EgoForm.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.FamilyPe.defaultMessage: An interface where participants draw their family: they select a person and add that person’s parents, siblings, partners or children, describing each new person as they go.
architect.interface.description.FamilyPe.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.FinishSe.defaultMessage: A screen that ends the interview. Add more than one to end it in different ways, such as a separate ending for participants who are not eligible.
architect.interface.description.FinishSe.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser. Stages that end the interview always sit together at the end of the protocol.

architect.interface.description.Geospati.defaultMessage: An interface that captures geospatial data by allowing the user to select items on a map
architect.interface.description.Geospati.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Informat.defaultMessage: A general purpose screen that can be used to present information to participants using a variety of text and media resources.
architect.interface.description.Informat.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Language.defaultMessage: A screen where participants choose the language for the rest of the interview, from the languages your protocol offers.
architect.interface.description.Language.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.NameGene.defaultMessage: A name generator interface which provides a form that participants complete when creating an alter.
architect.interface.description.NameGene.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.NameGene.defaultMessage: A name generator interface designed for low response-burden. Only requires a label in order to create an alter.
architect.interface.description.NameGene.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.NameGene.defaultMessage: A name generator specifically for roster data, allowing sorting and filtering of the roster.
architect.interface.description.NameGene.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Narrativ.defaultMessage: A qualitative interface that uses "presets" to switch between different views of the data in the network.
architect.interface.description.Narrativ.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Narrativ.defaultMessage: A read-only visualisation interface that overlays disease status and inheritance patterns onto a family pedigree collected by a Family Pedigree stage.
architect.interface.description.Narrativ.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.NetworkC.defaultMessage: A free-form, single-screen canvas for building a whole network — create nodes, draw multiple edge types, and capture node and edge attributes in one place.
architect.interface.description.NetworkC.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.OneToMan.defaultMessage: A name interpreter interface that creates edges by systematically surveying one alter against many others in the interview network.
architect.interface.description.OneToMan.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.OrdinalB.defaultMessage: A name interpreter interface that captures ordinal data by allowing the participant to drag and drop alters into bins.
architect.interface.description.OrdinalB.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.Sociogra.defaultMessage: Designed for spatially arranging alters (either manually or automatically), creating edges between them, and highlighting the presence of alter attributes.
architect.interface.description.Sociogra.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.interface.description.TieStren.defaultMessage: Combines a dyad census with an ordinal attribute to simultaneously capture the strength of ties between alters.
architect.interface.description.TieStren.description: Description of the interview interface in the New Stage chooser.

architect.issues.issues.description: Label of the toolbar button, and heading of the list it opens, showing how many problems must be fixed in the open stage. issueCount is that number.

architect.jsonPreviewOverlay.altShiftJTo.description: Hint in the header of the developer JSON preview overlay naming the keyboard shortcut that closes it.

architect.jsonPreviewOverlay.closePrevie.description: Accessible name of the full-screen backdrop button that closes the developer JSON preview overlay; read only by screen readers.

architect.jsonPreviewOverlay.copied.description: Text of the copy button in the developer JSON preview overlay for two seconds after the JSON was copied to the clipboard, confirming it worked.

architect.jsonPreviewOverlay.copy.description: Button in the developer JSON preview overlay that copies the displayed JSON to the clipboard.

architect.labelCollisions.description.defaultMessage: Participants could not tell these apart. The protocol can’t be downloaded until each pair has different labels.
architect.labelCollisions.description.description: Shown under the title of the warning about labels that are the same, above the list of pairs. “These” and “each pair” are the pairs of answer options or diseases listed below it. Researcher-facing.

architect.labelCollisions.diseasePair.defaultMessage: Diseases {first, number} and {second, number} of the stage “{stage}” have the same label in {language}: “{firstLabel}” and “{secondLabel}”.
architect.labelCollisions.diseasePair.description: One item in the warning about labels that are the same: two diseases (conditions a participant reports for their family members) of a Narrative Pedigree stage whose labels a participant reading the language would see as the same text. first and second are the diseases’ positions in the stage’s list, counting from 1. stage is the stage’s name. language is the name of the language, for example “Spanish”. firstLabel and secondLabel are the two labels as a participant reads them in that language; they may differ only in capital letters or spaces.

architect.labelCollisions.downloadRefuse.defaultMessage: Some answer options or diseases have the same label in one of the protocol’s languages, so participants could not tell them apart. The Stages page lists them. The protocol can’t be downloaded until each pair has different labels.
architect.labelCollisions.downloadRefuse.description: Shown in the dialog that refuses to download (or send) a protocol while two answer options of one attribute, or two diseases of a Narrative Pedigree stage, have the same label in one of the protocol’s languages, as a participant would see it: written the same, differing only in capital letters or spaces at either end, or because one has no translation in that language and shows another language’s text instead. Researcher-facing. “The Stages page” is the Architect page listing the protocol’s stages, where a notice names each pair.

architect.labelCollisions.editAttribute.description: Link after an item in the warning about labels that are the same, when the two options have the same label in the protocol’s default language. It opens the codebook editor where the attribute’s options are edited. attribute is the attribute’s name.

architect.labelCollisions.editStage.description: Link after an item in the warning about labels that are the same, when the two diseases have the same label in the protocol’s default language. It opens the editor of the stage the diseases belong to. stage is the stage’s name.

architect.labelCollisions.optionPair.defaultMessage: Options {first, number} and {second, number} of the attribute “{attribute}” have the same label in {language}: “{firstLabel}” and “{secondLabel}”.
architect.labelCollisions.optionPair.description: One item in the warning about labels that are the same: two answer options of one attribute (a question in the codebook with a fixed list of answers) whose labels a participant reading the language would see as the same text. first and second are the options’ positions in the attribute’s list, counting from 1. attribute is the attribute’s name. language is the name of the language, for example “Spanish”. firstLabel and secondLabel are the two labels as a participant reads them in that language; they may differ only in capital letters or spaces.

architect.labelCollisions.title.description: Title of the warning on the stage list shown while two answer options of one attribute, or two diseases of a Narrative Pedigree stage, have the same label in one of the protocol’s languages: a participant would see the same text, perhaps differing only in capital letters or spaces at either end. Researcher-facing.

architect.labelCollisions.translate.description: Link after an item in the warning about labels that are the same, when the two labels are the same only in a language other than the protocol’s default language, often because one of them has no translation into it. It opens the translation table showing that language beside the default one. language is the name of that language, for example “Spanish”.

architect.legacyProtocol.couldNotOpenInA.description: Title of the error dialog shown when a protocol file could not be passed to the previous version of Architect. {version} is that version’s number (for example 8).

architect.legacyProtocol.handoffFailed.defaultMessage: Architect could not prepare this file for Architect {version}. This can happen if storage on this device is full or unavailable. Your file has not been changed.
architect.legacyProtocol.handoffFailed.description: Error dialog text shown when a protocol file could not be passed to the previous version of Architect, because it could not be saved temporarily on this device. {version} is that version’s number (for example 8).

architect.legacyProtocol.keepEditingAsSc.description: Button in the dialog shown when opening an older protocol. Leaves the protocol unchanged and opens it in the previous version of Architect, which edits that schema. {version} is the older schema version number (for example 8).

architect.legacyProtocol.openInArchitect.description: Menu item on an older protocol in the home screen library. Opens the protocol, unchanged, in the previous version of Architect. {version} is that version’s number (for example 8).

architect.legacyProtocol.schemaBadge.description: Short badge on a protocol in the home screen library, marking a protocol made for an older schema version. {version} is that protocol’s schema version number (for example 8).

architect.legacyProtocol.upgradeToSchema.description: Button and menu item that creates an upgraded copy of an older protocol at the current schema version and opens it. {version} is the current schema version number (for example 9).

architect.library.metadata.justNow.description: Time shown on a protocol row of the start screen for a change made less than a minute ago. The less-than sign is part of the text.

architect.library.metadata.protocolMeta.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# stage} other {# stages}} · Added {created} · Edited {updated}
architect.library.metadata.protocolMeta.description: Summary line on a protocol row of the start screen. count is the number of stages; created is the date added; updated is the date last edited.

architect.library.metadata.templateMeta.defaultMessage: {stages, plural, one {# stage} other {# stages}} · {nodes, plural, one {# node type} other {# node types}} · {edges, plural, one {# edge type} other {# edge types}}
architect.library.metadata.templateMeta.description: Summary line on a template row of the start screen. stages is the number of stages; nodes is the number of node types; edges is the number of edge types.

architect.localization.addBaseLanguage.c.description: Button that declines the offer: the regional variant the researcher chose is still added (or the protocol still created in it), without also adding the language it belongs to. base is that language (for example Spanish).
Button that also adds the language a regional variant belongs to, as another of the protocol’s languages. base is that language (for example Spanish).

architect.localization.addBaseLanguage.d.defaultMessage: Network Canvas has built-in wording, such as button labels and the closing screen, in {base} but not in {language}. If you also add {base}, participants using {language} see the {base} wording wherever you haven’t written your own.{isDefault, select, true { Because {language} is the default language, the protocol can’t be downloaded until its built-in wording is translated into {language}, or {base} is made the default.} other {}}
architect.localization.addBaseLanguage.d.description: Explanation in the question asked when a regional variant of a language Network Canvas has built-in wording in is added to a protocol. language is the added language (for example Mexican Spanish); base is the language it is a variant of (for example Spanish). Adding the base language as a second language lets the interview show its built-in wording in place of any the researcher has not written for the variant. isDefault is true when the added language is the protocol’s default language, whose text must be complete before the protocol can be downloaded.

architect.localization.addBaseLanguage.t.description: Title of the question asked when the researcher adds a language to a protocol that Network Canvas has no built-in wording in, but that is a regional variant of a language it has wording in. base is that language (for example Spanish, when the added language is Mexican Spanish).

architect.localization.languageActions.a.defaultMessage: Participants can take the interview in any of the protocol’s languages. Until you translate the wording into a new language, participants who use it see the closest translation available instead.
architect.localization.languageActions.a.description: Explanation in the dialog that adds languages to a protocol.
Submit button of the dialog that adds languages.
Title of the dialog that adds languages to a protocol.

architect.localization.languageActions.c.defaultMessage: Use this when the wording recorded as {language} is really written in another language, for example in a protocol upgraded from an older version. Everything recorded as {language} is recorded as the language you choose instead. Wording you wrote or changed moves as it is, without being translated or deleted. Built-in wording you haven’t changed becomes Network Canvas’s version of it in the language you choose. Any built-in wording that Network Canvas doesn’t have in that language is removed, and you’ll need to write it.
architect.localization.languageActions.c.description: Explanation in the dialog that records the translations of one protocol language as another language. language is the name of the language being changed. Built-in wording is the text Network Canvas supplies, such as button labels and the closing screen. Text the researcher wrote, or built-in wording they reworded, keeps its words and moves to the chosen language. Built-in wording they have not changed is replaced, item by item, with Network Canvas’s wording in the chosen language; an item Network Canvas has no wording for in that language is removed, and the researcher must write it.
Submit button of the dialog that records the translations of a protocol language as another language.
Title of the dialog that records the translations of one protocol language as another language. language is the name of the language being changed.
Placeholder of the list of languages that the translations of a protocol language can be recorded as.
Error when a dialog that asks for languages is submitted with none chosen.
Placeholder of a list of languages to choose several from.
Error when the dialog that records the translations of a protocol language as another language is submitted without a language.

architect.localization.languageActions.l.description: Label of the list of languages in the dialog that records the translations of a protocol language as another language.
One entry in a list of languages. name is the language name in the interface language; tag is its language code, such as "de" or "pt-BR".
Label of the searchable list of languages to add.

architect.localization.languageActions.n.description: Shown when a language search finds nothing.

architect.localization.languageActions.o.description: Last item of the list of chosen languages when the rest do not fit, as in "English, Spanish and 4 others". The list joins it with "and". count is how many chosen languages are not named.

architect.localization.languageActions.r.description: Confirm button that removes a language from a protocol.

architect.localization.languageActions.r.defaultMessage: {count, plural, =0 {There are no {language} translations yet, so nothing will be deleted.} one {The # translation written in {language} will be deleted.} other {All # translations written in {language} will be deleted.}} Participants will no longer be able to choose this language.
architect.localization.languageActions.r.description: Confirmation before a language is removed. count is how many translations are deleted; language is the language name.
Title of the confirmation before a language is removed from a protocol.

architect.localization.languageActions.s.defaultMessage: Search languages or type a language code
architect.localization.languageActions.s.description: Placeholder of the search box in the list of languages. A language that is not in the list can be added by typing its language code, such as "haw" or "es-419".

architect.localization.languageChooserAl.defaultMessage: This protocol has more than one language but no Language Chooser stage. Each interview opens in the language that best matches the participant’s browser settings. Add a Language Chooser stage if participants should choose the language themselves.
architect.localization.languageChooserAl.description: Note shown while the protocol has more than one language but no Language Chooser stage. "Language Chooser" is the name of a stage type in the list of stages a researcher can add, so translate it the same way as that name.

architect.localization.languageChooserAl.defaultMessage: Dismiss the note that participants can’t choose a language
architect.localization.languageChooserAl.description: Accessible name of the button that hides the note saying participants can’t choose a language. The note stays hidden for this protocol.
Title of the note on the stage list shown while the protocol has more than one language but no Language Chooser stage.

architect.localization.languageList.addL.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding languages.

architect.localization.languageList.chan.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the button, with a two-way arrows icon, in a protocol language’s row. It opens a dialog that records the translations written in that language as another language, for translations recorded under the wrong one. language is the language name.

architect.localization.languageList.cove.defaultMessage: {translated, number} of {total, plural, one {# string} other {# strings}} translated
architect.localization.languageList.cove.description: How much of a protocol is translated into one language. total is the number of localized strings in the protocol.
Accessible name of the progress bar of one language.

architect.localization.languageList.defa.description: Badge marking the default language of a protocol.
Label of the list above the protocol languages that chooses which of them is the default.

architect.localization.languageList.defa.defaultMessage: Participants see this language wherever there is no translation in a language they use.
architect.localization.languageList.defa.description: Hint under the list that chooses the protocol’s default language, saying what the default language does.

architect.localization.languageList.defa.defaultMessage: To remove the default language, make another language the default first.
architect.localization.languageList.defa.description: Tooltip and accessible description of the unavailable delete button of the default language, saying why it cannot be removed.

architect.localization.languageList.desc.defaultMessage: Participants can take the interview in any of these languages. Where something is not translated, they see the first of the following languages that has a translation:
architect.localization.languageList.desc.description: Introduction to the list of protocol languages, shown when the protocol has more than one. Its second sentence introduces a numbered list, under it, of the languages a participant may see, in the order they are tried where something is not translated. The list of protocol languages is in alphabetical order; its order has no effect on which language participants see.

architect.localization.languageList.desc.defaultMessage: Participants take the interview in this language. Add more languages to let them choose one.
architect.localization.languageList.desc.description: Explanation of the list of protocol languages, shown when the protocol has only one language.

architect.localization.languageList.edit.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the edit button, with a pencil icon, in a protocol language’s row. It opens the translation table showing that language beside the default language, where its translations can be written and changed. language is the language name.

architect.localization.languageList.miss.description: Badge on a protocol language that some localized strings have not been translated into yet.

architect.localization.languageList.noTe.defaultMessage: There is nothing to translate yet.
architect.localization.languageList.noTe.description: Shown instead of translation progress in an empty protocol.

architect.localization.languageList.open.description: Link under the list of protocol languages to the translation table, which shows every participant-facing localized string beside its translation into each language.

architect.localization.languageList.remo.description: Accessible name of the delete button at the end of a protocol language’s row, which removes that language from the protocol. language is the language name.

architect.localization.languageList.stra.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {# string has a translation only in {language}. Translate it into another language before removing {language}.} other {# strings have a translation only in {language}. Translate them into another language before removing {language}.}}
architect.localization.languageList.stra.description: Tooltip and accessible description of the unavailable delete button of a language, saying why it cannot be removed: some localized strings have no translation in another language.

architect.localization.languageList.titl.description: Heading of the list of languages a protocol is written in.

architect.localization.localizationAlert.defaultMessage: Dismiss the note about missing translations
architect.localization.localizationAlert.description: Accessible name of the button that hides the note about missing translations on the stage list. The note comes back if more translations go missing.

architect.localization.localizationAlert.defaultMessage: Some wording isn’t translated into {languages} yet. Participants see it in another language instead.
architect.localization.localizationAlert.description: Notice shown while some of the protocol’s wording has no translation in one or more of its languages. languages is the list of those languages, already joined in the reader’s language, for example “French, German and Tibetan”.
Title of the informational notice on the stage list shown while some of the protocol’s wording has no translation in one or more of its languages.
Link in the note about missing translations on the stage list. It opens the translation table showing only the localized strings with a translation missing.

architect.localization.textPlaces.edgeTy.description: Kind of codebook entry that holds a group of texts in the translation table, before the entry’s name: an edge type.

architect.localization.textPlaces.ego.description: Heading of the group of texts in the translation table that belong to the ego (the participant) in the codebook.

architect.localization.textPlaces.interf.description: Heading of the group of texts in the translation table that the interview itself shows, such as its buttons and messages, rather than text written for a stage or codebook entry.

architect.localization.textPlaces.nodeTy.description: Kind of codebook entry that holds a group of texts in the translation table, before the entry’s name: a node type.

architect.localization.textPlaces.protoc.description: Heading of the group of texts in the translation table that belong to the protocol itself rather than to a stage or codebook entry.

architect.localization.textPlaces.stageP.description: Names the stage that holds a group of texts in the translation table, before the stage’s name. position is the stage’s place in the protocol, counting from 1.

architect.localization.textPlaces.unname.description: Shown in the translation table in place of the name of a stage or type that has no name.

architect.localization.translationFallba.defaultMessage: Any other language that has a translation.
architect.localization.translationFallba.description: Last item of the numbered list of the languages a participant may see, in the order they are tried.

architect.localization.translationFallba.defaultMessage: Another language their browser or device lists.
architect.localization.translationFallba.description: Third item of the numbered list of the languages a participant may see, in the order they are tried.
Fourth item of the numbered list of the languages a participant may see, in the order they are tried.

architect.localization.translationFallba.defaultMessage: Their own language: the one they chose, or the one their browser or device is set to.
architect.localization.translationFallba.description: First item of the numbered list of the languages a participant may see, in the order they are tried.
Link to the documentation guide about translating a protocol. The text inside <link> is the guide’s title.

architect.localization.translationFallba.defaultMessage: A closely related language, such as Brazilian Portuguese for a participant using European Portuguese.
architect.localization.translationFallba.description: Second item of the numbered list of the languages a participant may see, in the order they are tried.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: This table shows everything participants see in the interview, with its translation into each language. Where a translation is missing, the cell shows what participants see instead.
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Opening paragraph of the help for the translation table, which explains what the table shows.
Option in the menu above the translation table that shows every localized string the protocol has.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: Everything is translated into the languages shown.
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Shown in the translation table when only localized strings with missing translations are shown and there are none.
Shown in the translation table when only localized strings with no translation into one language are shown and there are none. language is the language’s name, such as “French”.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: Everything participants see, with its translation into each of the protocol’s languages
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Caption of the translation table, read by screen readers. Each row is one localized string, each column one language.
Badge beside the name of the protocol’s default language, in the heading of its column in the translation table.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: Another disease has the same name in {language}. Give each disease a name participants can tell apart.
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Shown in a cell of the translation table holding a disease’s name, on a Narrative Pedigree stage, when participants reading the cell’s language would see the same name for another disease, either because it is written the same or because one of them has no translation and shows another language’s text instead. language is the cell’s language.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: Another option of this attribute has the same label in {language}. Give each option a label participants can tell apart.
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Shown in a cell of the translation table holding the label of one of an attribute’s answer options (including the two answers of a yes-or-no attribute), when participants reading the cell’s language would see the same label for another option of the same attribute, either because it is written the same or because one of them has no translation and shows another language’s text instead. language is the cell’s language.
Accessible name of the menu above the translation table that chooses whether it shows every localized string or only those with a translation missing.

Heading of a group of rows in the translation table, naming the codebook entry that holds their localized strings. place is the kind of entry, such as “Node type”; name is its name, which links to it. Keep the tags around the same parts.

Heading of a group of rows in the translation table, naming the stage that holds their localized strings. place is the stage’s position, such as “Stage 4”; name is the stage’s name, which links to it; detail is the kind of stage, such as “Name Generator”. Keep the tags around the same parts.
Button in the toolbar of the translation table that opens a short explanation of the table and how to edit it.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: This text needs words in {language}, the protocol’s default language.
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Shown in a cell of the translation table holding words the interview itself shows, such as a button’s label, when the cell is in the protocol’s default language and has been emptied: those words always need a translation in the default language. language is the default language.

architect.localization.translationTable..defaultMessage: Select a cell to edit it. Your changes are kept in the table until you select Save, and each cell is checked when you leave it. Press Escape to undo your changes to a cell. When the cursor is on the first or last line of a cell, the up and down arrow keys move to the previous or next row. Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) also moves to the next row, as Enter does in a cell with one line. In a cell with formatting, Tab moves to the formatting buttons and then to the next cell, except in a list, where it indents the item.
architect.localization.translationTable..description: Help text for the translation table, explaining how editing its cells works. Nothing typed into the table reaches the protocol until the researcher selects Save. Ctrl, Enter, ⌘, Escape and Tab are the names of keys; use the names printed on keyboards in your language. A cell with formatting holds text with bold, italics, headings or lists, which is edited with a row of formatting buttons above it.
Button above the translation table that opens a menu for showing and hiding language columns. shown is how many languages are shown, total how many the protocol has.
Heading of the menu that shows and hides the language columns of the translation table.
Note in the menu of language columns when only one language is shown, which therefore cannot be hidden.
