architect.protocolOpenDialogs.technicalD.description: Label of the collapsed section, in an error dialog about opening a protocol, that holds the underlying error text. The text inside is always English, which the label says.

architect.protocolOpenDialogs.upgradeAff.defaultMessage: Please note: upgrading may change the interview experience for participants, and will require you to also use the latest version of Interviewer or Fresco.
architect.protocolOpenDialogs.upgradeAff.description: Paragraph in the dialog offering to upgrade an older protocol to the current schema. Warns that interviews may look or behave differently after upgrading, and that the upgraded protocol only runs in the latest versions of Interviewer and Fresco (the apps that run interviews). <strong> wraps the opening words, shown in bold.

architect.protocolOpenDialogs.upgradeCha.defaultMessage: If you upgrade, the following changes will be made to your protocol:
architect.protocolOpenDialogs.upgradeCha.description: Sentence in the dialog offering to upgrade an older protocol, introducing the box below it that lists every change the upgrade makes to the protocol.

architect.protocolOpenDialogs.upgradeMak.defaultMessage: Upgrading creates a separate copy of your protocol and opens it. Your original protocol will not be changed.
architect.protocolOpenDialogs.upgradeMak.description: Paragraph in the dialog offering to upgrade an older protocol to the current schema. Explains that upgrading makes a new copy at the current schema and opens it, and that the original protocol stays as it was.

architect.protocolReview.availability.av.description: Why a review cannot be started: the budget of every provider that could write the review is spent, for the day or the month. {when} is the moment the first of them starts again, such as "tomorrow at 01:00" or "1 Dec 2026 at 01:00".

architect.protocolReview.availability.ne.description: Why a review cannot be started: the hourly limit is used up. {when} is a time such as "today at 15:32".

architect.protocolReview.availability.of.description: Why a review cannot be started: there is no internet connection.

architect.protocolReview.button.failed.defaultMessage: Protocol review could not be completed. Open Review protocol to see why.
architect.protocolReview.button.failed.description: Read by screen readers when an automated review fails. "Review protocol" is the name of the toolbar button and must match its translation.

architect.protocolReview.button.finished.defaultMessage: Protocol review finished. {count, plural, =0 {It found no problems.} one {It found # problem.} other {It found # problems.}}
architect.protocolReview.button.finished.description: Read by screen readers when an automated review finishes. {count} is how many problems it found.

architect.protocolReview.button.notStart.defaultMessage: The review could not start. Review protocol says why.
architect.protocolReview.button.notStart.description: Read by screen readers when a review could not start (offline, the hourly limit, or another reason shown in the panel). "Review protocol" is the name of the toolbar button.

architect.protocolReview.button.reviewPr.description: Toolbar button on the Stages screen that opens the automated protocol review.

architect.protocolReview.button.reviewin.description: Label of the Review protocol toolbar button while an automated review runs.

architect.protocolReview.button.undecide.defaultMessage: Review protocol, {count, plural, one {# problem still to decide} other {# problems still to decide}}
architect.protocolReview.button.undecide.description: Accessible name, read by screen readers, of the Review protocol toolbar button while it shows a count badge. It must start with the button’s visible text ("Review protocol", as translated for that button). {count} is how many problems from the last review the researcher has not decided about.

architect.protocolReview.category.attrib.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: the variables recorded and the forms that ask for them. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.category.burden.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: how long or tiring the interview is for participants. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.category.entiti.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: the node and edge types of the codebook. "Node" and "edge" are Network Canvas terms for people (or things) and the connections between them, as Architect names them elsewhere. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.category.resear.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: whether the interview answers the researcher’s research questions. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.category.skipLo.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: rules that skip stages or filter who appears on them. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.category.struct.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: the order and kinds of stages in the interview. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.category.wordin.description: Which part of the study design a problem found by the automated protocol review is about: how prompts and instructions are worded. Shown as a label on one problem.

architect.protocolReview.location.codebo.description: Where in the protocol a problem found by the automated protocol review is: the codebook as a whole. "Codebook" is the name of a page in Architect.

Where in the protocol a problem found by the automated protocol review is: the variables about the participant themselves ("Ego", as the Codebook page names them). "Codebook" is the name of a page in Architect. The dot is a separator.

Where in the protocol a problem found by the automated protocol review is: one node or edge type in the codebook. {typeName} is the type’s name as the researcher wrote it. "Codebook" is the name of a page in Architect. The dot is a separator.

architect.protocolReview.location.openCo.description: Link from a problem found by the automated protocol review to the Codebook page, where the researcher will fix it themselves.

architect.protocolReview.location.openSt.description: Link from a problem found by the automated protocol review to the stage it is about, which the researcher will fix themselves. {position} is the stage’s number on the Stages screen.

architect.protocolReview.location.protoc.description: Where in the protocol a problem found by the automated protocol review is: no one stage or type, but the protocol as a whole.

architect.protocolReview.location.stage.description: Where in the protocol a problem found by the automated protocol review is: one stage. {position} is the stage’s number on the Stages screen; {label} is the stage’s name as the researcher wrote it. The dot is a separator.

architect.protocolReview.notice.allSpent.defaultMessage: This is a free experimental service with a fixed budget for each provider, shared by everyone who uses it. Every provider’s budget has been spent.
architect.protocolReview.notice.allSpent.description: Text of the notice shown when the budget of every provider is spent. A provider is the company whose AI model writes the review (Anthropic or OpenAI).

architect.protocolReview.notice.allSpent.defaultMessage: Protocol review has reached its limit
architect.protocolReview.notice.allSpent.description: Title of the notice shown when the budget of every provider is spent, so no review can start for now.

architect.protocolReview.notice.budgetBo.defaultMessage: This is a free experimental service with a fixed budget for each provider, shared by everyone who uses it. Start the review again to choose another model. Nothing in your protocol was changed.
architect.protocolReview.notice.budgetBo.description: Text of the notice shown when the chosen provider’s budget is spent and another provider still has budget. A provider is the company whose AI model writes the review (Anthropic or OpenAI); the researcher chooses a model in the last step of the dialog that starts a review.

architect.protocolReview.notice.budgetTi.defaultMessage: The budget for {company} has been spent
architect.protocolReview.notice.budgetTi.description: Title of the notice shown when a review could not start because the budget of the provider chosen to write it is spent. {company} is the provider’s name, "Anthropic" or "OpenAI", and is not translated.

architect.protocolReview.notice.dismiss.description: Button that hides the notice about a review that could not be completed.

architect.protocolReview.notice.hourlyBo.defaultMessage: You can review again {when}. The limit keeps this free service available to everyone.
architect.protocolReview.notice.hourlyBo.description: Text of the hourly limit notice. {when} is a moment such as "today at 15:32".

architect.protocolReview.notice.hourlyTi.defaultMessage: You have used your {limit, plural, one {# review} other {# reviews}} for this hour
architect.protocolReview.notice.hourlyTi.description: Title of the notice shown when the researcher has started as many reviews as are allowed in an hour. {limit} is that number.

architect.protocolReview.notice.offlineB.defaultMessage: Protocol review needs an internet connection. You can review this protocol when you are back online.
architect.protocolReview.notice.offlineB.description: Text of the offline notice, shown in the review panel while the protocol has no review.

architect.protocolReview.notice.offlineT.description: Title of the notice shown when there is no internet connection.

architect.protocolReview.notice.tooLarge.defaultMessage: The review service only accepts protocols up to a fixed size, and this one is larger. Nothing in your protocol was changed, and this attempt did not count towards your limit.
This protocol is too large to review
architect.protocolReview.notice.tooLarge.description: Title of the notice shown when the protocol is larger than the review service accepts.

architect.protocolReview.notice.unavaila.defaultMessage: The problem is with the review service, not with your protocol or your connection, and the Network Canvas team has been told. Nothing in your protocol was changed, and this attempt did not count towards your limit.
architect.protocolReview.notice.unavaila.description: Text of the service unavailable notice. "Network Canvas" is a product name and is not translated.

architect.protocolReview.notice.unavaila.defaultMessage: Protocol review is not available right now
architect.protocolReview.notice.unavaila.description: Title of the notice shown when the review service failed or refused the request.

architect.protocolReview.popover.cancelR.description: Button that stops the review in progress. Nothing is saved and it does not count towards the hourly limit.

architect.protocolReview.popover.dismiss.defaultMessage: The review could not be dismissed, because this protocol is open for editing in another tab. Dismiss it in that tab.
architect.protocolReview.popover.dismiss.description: Notice when Dismiss review was refused because another browser tab holds this protocol for editing.
Button under the list of problems that removes the review. The protocol is then as if it had not been reviewed, and a new review can be started.
Status of a problem the researcher dismissed.

architect.protocolReview.popover.fixUndo.description: Read by screen readers after Undo in the review list took a fix back out of the protocol. {title} is the problem’s title, written by the review service.

architect.protocolReview.popover.fixed.description: Status of a problem whose suggested fix was made in the protocol by Architect.

architect.protocolReview.popover.goThrou.defaultMessage: Go through {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}
architect.protocolReview.popover.goThrou.description: Button that opens the problems still to decide one at a time. {count} is how many there are.

architect.protocolReview.popover.meta.description: A problem’s severity and where it is, under its title in the list. {severity} is a word such as "Serious"; {location} is a place such as "Stage 10 · Who knows whom". The dot is a separator.

architect.protocolReview.popover.mine.description: Status of a problem the researcher chose to fix themselves ("I will fix this").

architect.protocolReview.popover.noProbl.description: Shown in place of the list when a review found nothing.

architect.protocolReview.popover.notRevi.description: Line under the Protocol review heading before the protocol has ever been reviewed.

architect.protocolReview.popover.phaseTh.defaultMessage: The reviewer is reading your protocol and thinking it through.
architect.protocolReview.popover.phaseTh.description: Line under the progress bar during the first part of an automated review, before the reviewer (an AI model) has begun writing its answer.

architect.protocolReview.popover.phaseWr.defaultMessage: The reviewer is writing up what it found.
architect.protocolReview.popover.phaseWr.description: Line under the progress bar during the second part of an automated review, while the reviewer (an AI model) writes its answer.

architect.protocolReview.popover.problem.description: Accessible name, read by screen readers, of the list of problems the review found.

architect.protocolReview.popover.progres.description: Accessible name, read by screen readers, of the progress bar shown while an automated review runs.

architect.protocolReview.popover.quota.defaultMessage: {remaining, number} of {limit, number} reviews left this hour
architect.protocolReview.popover.quota.description: Caption beside the review buttons: how many reviews the researcher may still start this hour.

architect.protocolReview.popover.ready.defaultMessage: A review lists the problems it finds in your protocol, most serious first. Nothing in your protocol changes until you choose.
architect.protocolReview.popover.ready.description: Shown in the review panel while the protocol has no review: what a review gives the researcher.

architect.protocolReview.popover.results.defaultMessage: The results of your review are shown below in order of importance.
architect.protocolReview.popover.results.description: Line under the Protocol review heading, above the list of problems the review found.

architect.protocolReview.popover.reviewD.description: Read by screen readers after Dismiss review removed the review.

architect.protocolReview.popover.running.defaultMessage: This can take a few minutes. You can close this panel and keep working. While the panel is closed, the button shows how far the review has got, then a count of the problems found.
architect.protocolReview.popover.running.description: Text while an automated review runs. "The button" is the Review protocol toolbar button.

architect.protocolReview.popover.running.defaultMessage: Review {current, number} of {limit, number} this hour
architect.protocolReview.popover.running.description: Caption while a review runs: which of the researcher’s reviews allowed this hour it is.

architect.protocolReview.popover.running.defaultMessage: Reviewing {count, plural, one {# stage} other {# stages}} against your study details
architect.protocolReview.popover.running.description: Heading while an automated review runs. {count} is how many stages the protocol has.

architect.protocolReview.popover.startRe.description: Button in the review panel that opens the dialog a researcher goes through to start an automated review of the protocol.

architect.protocolReview.popover.started.description: Line under the Protocol review heading while a review runs. {time} is a time of day, already formatted.

architect.protocolReview.popover.title.description: Heading of the panel that opens from the Review protocol toolbar button, showing the automated protocol review.

architect.protocolReview.popover.tryAgai.description: Button that sends the same review again after the review service was not available.

architect.protocolReview.popover.undo.description: Button beside "Fixed for you" that takes the fix back out of the protocol.

architect.protocolReview.popover.undoDis.description: Button beside a dismissed problem in the review list that returns it to the problems still to decide.

architect.protocolReview.problem.afterFi.description: Label over a piece of text as the suggested fix would change it.

architect.protocolReview.problem.allDeci.defaultMessage: You have been through every problem. Back at the list of problems.
architect.protocolReview.problem.allDeci.description: Read by screen readers when the researcher decides about the last problem still open and the panel returns to the list of all the problems.

architect.protocolReview.problem.back.description: Button on one problem found by the automated protocol review that returns to the list of all the problems.

architect.protocolReview.problem.cannotF.defaultMessage: This fix cannot be made for you. Make the change yourself, using the description below.
architect.protocolReview.problem.cannotF.description: Notice on a problem whose suggested fix Architect cannot apply automatically.

architect.protocolReview.problem.changed.defaultMessage: This fix can no longer be made for you, because that part of the protocol changed after the review. Make the change yourself, using the description below.
architect.protocolReview.problem.changed.description: Notice on a problem whose suggested fix no longer fits the protocol, because the researcher has since changed what it would edit.

architect.protocolReview.problem.checkin.defaultMessage: Checking whether this fix can be made for you…
architect.protocolReview.problem.checkin.description: Read by screen readers with the Fix for me button while Architect works out whether the fix leaves a valid protocol.

architect.protocolReview.problem.concent.description: Names the number setting for how many circles a sociogram background shows, above a fix that changes it.

architect.protocolReview.problem.decideL.description: Button on a problem the researcher said they will fix themselves that returns it to the problems still to decide.

architect.protocolReview.problem.dismiss.description: Button that puts a problem found by the automated protocol review away without changing anything, and moves to the next problem.
Notice on a problem the researcher already dismissed.

architect.protocolReview.problem.editVal.description: Button in the After the fix box that lets the researcher change the suggested text or number before the fix is made.

architect.protocolReview.problem.editedI.defaultMessage: Your changes would leave the protocol invalid. Change them, or use the suggestion.
architect.protocolReview.problem.editedI.description: Notice when Fix for me is pressed with text or numbers the researcher changed, and the result would not be a valid protocol.

architect.protocolReview.problem.fixAppl.description: Read by screen readers after Fix for me changed the protocol. {title} is the problem’s title, written by the review service.

architect.protocolReview.problem.fixForM.description: Button that makes the suggested fix in the protocol now (it can be undone), and moves to the next problem.

architect.protocolReview.problem.fixUndo.description: Read by screen readers after a fix made for the researcher was taken back out. {title} is the problem’s title, written by the review service.

architect.protocolReview.problem.fixedNo.defaultMessage: This was fixed for you. You have changed that part of the protocol since, so the fix cannot be undone from here; use Undo in the toolbar instead.
architect.protocolReview.problem.fixedNo.description: Notice on a problem fixed for the researcher whose change can no longer be taken back from the review, only with the app’s ordinary Undo button.

architect.protocolReview.problem.fixedSt.defaultMessage: This was fixed for you. Undo takes the change back out of your protocol.
architect.protocolReview.problem.fixedSt.description: Notice on a problem the researcher already chose Fix for me for, while that change is still in the protocol. "Undo" is the name of a button.

architect.protocolReview.problem.maxNode.description: Names the number setting for the most nodes a participant may add on a stage, above a fix that changes it.

architect.protocolReview.problem.minNode.description: Names the number setting for the fewest nodes a participant must add on a stage, above a fix that changes it.

architect.protocolReview.problem.mine.description: Button that keeps a problem on the researcher’s list, for them to fix themselves, and moves to the next problem.

architect.protocolReview.problem.mineSta.defaultMessage: You chose to fix this yourself.
architect.protocolReview.problem.mineSta.description: Notice on a problem the researcher already chose "I will fix this" for.

architect.protocolReview.problem.nextPro.description: Button that moves on from a problem already fixed to the next problem still to decide.

architect.protocolReview.problem.notANum.description: Shown under a number the researcher is changing before the fix is made, when the field does not hold a number.

architect.protocolReview.problem.notOwne.defaultMessage: This protocol is open for editing in another tab, so it cannot be changed here. Make the change in that tab.
architect.protocolReview.problem.notOwne.description: Notice when Fix for me was refused because another browser tab holds this protocol for editing.

architect.protocolReview.problem.notSet.description: Shown in the Now box for a number setting, such as a limit on answers, that the protocol does not have yet.

architect.protocolReview.problem.notUpda.defaultMessage: That choice could not be saved, because the review changed in the meantime. Go back and open the problem again.
architect.protocolReview.problem.notUpda.description: Notice when a choice about a problem could not be recorded because the review it belongs to was replaced or the problem was already fixed. "Back" is the name of the button that returns to the list of problems.

architect.protocolReview.problem.now.description: Label over a piece of text as it is in the protocol now, shown beside the same text as the suggested fix would change it.

architect.protocolReview.problem.numberS.description: Names a number a fix changes, above its Now and After the fix boxes. {setting} is the setting, such as "Maximum selected"; {name} is the attribute or stage it belongs to. The dot is a separator.

architect.protocolReview.problem.otherTr.defaultMessage: This protocol also has this text in {languages}. Fix for me does not change {count, plural, one {that version} other {those versions}}, so check {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} after the fix.
architect.protocolReview.problem.otherTr.description: Note under a suggested change to a text that the protocol also has in other languages. {languages} is a list of language names, already joined for the reader’s language (for example "Spanish and French"); {count} is how many. "Fix for me" is the name of a button and must match its translation.

architect.protocolReview.problem.problem.description: Shows which problem found by the automated protocol review is open, when going through them one at a time.

architect.protocolReview.problem.suggest.description: Heading of the part of a problem that describes how the automated protocol review suggests fixing it.

architect.protocolReview.problem.undo.description: Button that takes a fix made for the researcher back out of the protocol.

architect.protocolReview.problem.undoDis.description: Button on a problem the researcher dismissed that returns it to the problems still to decide.

architect.protocolReview.problem.useSugg.description: Button that puts back the suggested text or number after the researcher changed it, before the fix is made.

architect.protocolReview.progressRing.la.description: Accessible name, read by screen readers, of the small circular progress indicator on the Review protocol toolbar button while an automated protocol review runs.

architect.protocolReview.severity.seriou.description: How serious a problem the automated protocol review found is: the most serious of three levels. Shown beside the problem’s title in the review results.

architect.protocolReview.severity.sugges.description: How serious a problem the automated protocol review found is: the least serious of three levels, an idea rather than a fault. Shown beside the problem’s title in the review results.

architect.protocolReview.severity.worthF.description: How serious a problem the automated protocol review found is: the middle of three levels. Shown beside the problem’s title in the review results.

architect.protocolReview.when.defaultMessage: {day, select, today {today at {time}} yesterday {yesterday at {time}} tomorrow {tomorrow at {time}} other {{date} at {time}}}
architect.protocolReview.when.description: A moment, said relative to today, used inside other protocol review sentences such as "Reviewed {when}" and "You can review again {when}". The sentence around it adds no "at" or "on" of its own. {time} is a time of day and {date} a date, both already formatted for the reader’s language. Keep the four cases (today, yesterday, tomorrow, other) as they are; translate only the words inside them.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.before.d.defaultMessage: This experimental feature uses LLMs (also known as ‘AI’) to generate review feedback to help you improve your protocol. To use this feature, your protocol must be sent to one of the providers we support (Anthropic and OpenAI). Ensure that you are permitted to do this by your IRB or ethics review body.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.before.d.description: Text of the first step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review. An LLM is a large language model. "Anthropic" and "OpenAI" are company names and are not translated. An IRB is an institutional review board, the body that approves research involving people.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.before.s.defaultMessage: What is sent for review, and what is never sent
architect.protocolReview.wizard.before.s.description: Accessible name, read by screen readers, of the two-column table listing what the automated protocol review sends and what it never sends.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.before.t.description: Heading of the first step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review. It says what the feature does, what it sends, and asks whether the review may be shared.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.al.defaultMessage: This is a free experimental service with a fixed budget for each provider, shared by everyone who uses it. Every provider’s budget has been spent, so a review cannot start for now. Save your study details now, and start the review once a budget starts again.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.al.description: Notice on the last step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review, when no model can be chosen because every provider’s budget is spent. The button below it then reads "Save details" in place of "Start review".

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.by.description: Line under a model’s name in the choice of AI model. {company} is the company that makes it, "Anthropic" or "OpenAI", and is not translated.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.de.defaultMessage: Your protocol and study details are sent to the provider of the model you choose, and that model writes the review. A review can take several minutes.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.de.description: Explanation under the heading of the last step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review. A provider is the company that makes an AI model (Anthropic or OpenAI).

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.la.description: Label of the choice between the AI models that can write the review.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.of.defaultMessage: You’re offline. Protocol review needs an internet connection; you can start the review when you are back online.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.of.description: Notice on the last step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review, when there is no internet connection.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.qu.defaultMessage: {remaining, number} of {limit, number} reviews left this hour
architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.qu.description: Note on the last step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review: how many reviews the researcher may still start this hour.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.sp.defaultMessage: The budget for {company} has been spent.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.sp.description: Why a model cannot be chosen to write the review, when the service did not say when its budget starts again. {company} is the company that makes it, "Anthropic" or "OpenAI", and is not translated.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.sp.defaultMessage: The budget for {company} has been spent. It starts again {when}.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.sp.description: Why a model cannot be chosen to write the review. {company} is the company that makes it, "Anthropic" or "OpenAI", and is not translated; {when} is a moment such as "tomorrow at 01:00" or "1 Dec 2026 at 01:00".

architect.protocolReview.wizard.model.ti.description: Heading of the last step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review: the choice of which AI model writes the review.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.description: Label of the choice between an interview run by an interviewer and one participants complete alone.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.defaultMessage: Choose how the interview is administered.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.description: Error under the administration choice when neither option is chosen and the researcher tries to continue.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.defaultMessage: We ask for information about your participants and how your interview will be administered so that the agent can identify issues with how tasks are explained, and the wording of prompts.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.description: Explanation under the heading of the participants step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review. "The agent" is the automated reviewer.
Option: an interviewer is with the participant during the interview.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.defaultMessage: An interviewer sits with the participant and can explain each task.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.description: Explanation under the Face to face option.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.defaultMessage: Who will be interviewed: eligibility criteria, age range, setting and how participants are recruited.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.description: Hint under the Research population label.
Label of the text box in which the researcher describes who takes part in their study.
Error under an empty Research population box when the researcher tries to continue.
Option: participants complete the interview on their own.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.defaultMessage: Participants complete the interview on their own, remotely or on a device handed to them.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.particip.description: Heading of the third step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.question.description: Button under the research questions that adds another, empty, question.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.question.defaultMessage: Research questions are optional, but recommended. With them, the automated reviewer can check whether your interview collects what each question needs. Without them, the problems it finds will be less specific. Only include research questions that are related to your Network Canvas interview.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.question.description: Explanation under the heading of the research questions step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review. "Network Canvas" is a product name and is not translated.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.question.defaultMessage: Up to {max, number} characters each. A box left empty is not sent.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.question.description: Note under the research questions, saying how long each question may be and that an empty one is ignored. {max} is a number of characters.
Label of one research question’s text box. {number} counts the questions from 1.
Accessible name of the button beside a research question that removes it from the list. {number} counts the questions from 1.
Heading of the fourth step of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review. The step is optional.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.saveDeta.description: Last button of the dialog that starts an automated protocol review, in place of "Start review" when no review can start because every provider’s budget is spent: saves the study details the researcher entered, so they are filled in next time, and starts nothing.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..defaultMessage: API keys saved in your protocol
architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..description: Item in the list of what is never sent for review. An API key is a credential the researcher saved as a resource, for example a Mapbox key for a map stage.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..defaultMessage: Interview data. Architect never holds any.
architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..description: Item in the list of what is never sent for review. "Architect" is the product name and is not translated.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..defaultMessage: Images, video, audio and other resources
architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..description: Item in the list of what is never sent for review.
Item in the list of what is never sent for review.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..defaultMessage: The codebook: node types, edge types, attributes and their options
architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..description: Item in the list of what is sent for review. "Codebook" is the name of a page in Architect.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..defaultMessage: Stage names, prompts, forms and skip logic
architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..description: Item in the list of what is sent for review.

architect.protocolReview.wizard.sending..defaultMessage: The study details you give in the next three steps

architect.resource.genericImportFailure.defaultMessage: Check that it is a supported file type, and try again.
architect.resource.genericImportFailure.description: Advice shown in the import error dialog when a file fails to import for an unexpected reason: the file may not be a supported type.

architect.resourceImport.charactersInAtt.defaultMessage: An attribute name in node {node} contains a character that can’t be used ({character}). Delete it from the file, then import the file again.{others, plural, =0 {} one { The same problem appears in # other place in the file.} other { The same problem appears in # other places in the file.}}
architect.resourceImport.charactersInAtt.description: Error shown when an attribute name in a JSON network file added as a resource contains a character Network Canvas can’t store. node is the node’s position in the file’s list of nodes, counting from 1. character is the character’s Unicode code point, such as U+0007, and stays as written. It is usually an invisible control character pasted in from another program, which an exported file could not hold. others is how many more places in the file have the same problem; when it is 0 nothing more is said.

architect.resourceImport.charactersInAtt.defaultMessage: The “{attribute}” attribute of node {node} contains a character that can’t be used ({character}). Delete it from the file, then import the file again.{others, plural, =0 {} one { The same problem appears in # other place in the file.} other { The same problem appears in # other places in the file.}}
architect.resourceImport.charactersInAtt.description: Error shown when an attribute value in a JSON network file added as a resource contains a character Network Canvas can’t store. attribute is the attribute’s name as the file writes it; node is the node’s position in the file’s list of nodes, counting from 1. character is the character’s Unicode code point, such as U+0007, and stays as written. It is usually an invisible control character pasted in from another program, which an exported file could not hold. others is how many more places in the file have the same problem; when it is 0 nothing more is said.

architect.resourceImport.charactersInCel.defaultMessage: Row {row} of the “{column}” column contains a character that can’t be used ({character}). Delete it from the file, then import the file again.{others, plural, =0 {} one { The same problem appears in # other place in the file.} other { The same problem appears in # other places in the file.}}
architect.resourceImport.charactersInCel.description: Error shown when a cell of a CSV network file added as a resource contains a character Network Canvas can’t store. row is the row number a spreadsheet shows, where the header is row 1; column is the researcher’s own column header. character is the character’s Unicode code point, such as U+0007, and stays as written. It is usually an invisible control character pasted in from another program, which an exported file could not hold. others is how many more places in the file have the same problem; when it is 0 nothing more is said.

architect.resourceImport.charactersInCol.defaultMessage: The header of column {column} contains a character that can’t be used ({character}). Delete it from the file, then import the file again.{others, plural, =0 {} one { The same problem appears in # other place in the file.} other { The same problem appears in # other places in the file.}}
architect.resourceImport.charactersInCol.description: Error shown when the header of a column in a CSV network file added as a resource contains a character Network Canvas can’t store. column is the column’s position, counting from 1 at the left. character is the character’s Unicode code point, such as U+0007, and stays as written. It is usually an invisible control character pasted in from another program, which an exported file could not hold. others is how many more places in the file have the same problem; when it is 0 nothing more is said.

architect.resourceImport.charactersInLin.defaultMessage: Line {line} of this file contains a character that can’t be used ({character}). Delete it from the file, then import the file again.{others, plural, =0 {} one { The same problem appears in # other place in the file.} other { The same problem appears in # other places in the file.}}
architect.resourceImport.charactersInLin.description: Error shown when a network file (CSV or JSON) added as a resource contains a character Network Canvas can’t store, somewhere that can only be pointed to by its line. line is the line number a text editor shows, counting from 1. character is the character’s Unicode code point, such as U+0007, and stays as written. It is usually an invisible control character pasted in from another program, which an exported file could not hold. others is how many more places in the file have the same problem; when it is 0 nothing more is said.

architect.resourceImport.columns.defaultMessage: Some rows have a different number of columns. Make each row match the column headers, then import the file again.
architect.resourceImport.columns.description: Error shown when a CSV network file added as a resource has rows with a different number of columns from the header row.

architect.resourceImport.duplicateColumn.defaultMessage: Two column headers in this file are the same name written in two different ways, such as an accented letter typed as one character in one and as two in the other. Rename or remove one of them, then import the file again.
architect.resourceImport.duplicateColumn.description: Error shown when a network file (CSV or JSON) is added as a resource and two of its column headers look identical but are stored differently: the same accented letter is typed as a single character in one header and as a plain letter followed by a separate accent mark in the other. Network Canvas would treat them as one attribute and lose one column’s values. Headers that differ only in capital letters are not affected.

architect.resourceImport.empty.defaultMessage: This network file doesn't contain any nodes or edges.
architect.resourceImport.empty.description: Error shown when a network file (CSV or JSON) added as a resource contains no nodes or edges.

architect.resourceImport.generic.defaultMessage: Check that it is a supported file type, and try again.
architect.resourceImport.generic.description: Fallback error shown when adding a file as a resource fails for a reason that has no specific message. Suggests checking the file type and trying again.

architect.resourceImport.names.defaultMessage: Some column headers in this file can’t be used as attribute names. A header can’t be empty, can’t start or end with a space, and can’t contain tabs, line breaks or other control characters. Fix the headers, then import the file again.
architect.resourceImport.names.description: Error shown when a network file (CSV or JSON) is added as a resource and one of its attribute names, taken from the column headers, is not allowed. Any script, spaces and punctuation are allowed inside a name.

architect.resourceImport.replacementType.defaultMessage: This file is a different kind of resource from the one it would replace. Choose a file of the same kind, and try again.
architect.resourceImport.replacementType.description: Error shown when the researcher supplies a file to replace a missing resource, but the file is a different kind of resource (for example an image instead of a video) from the one it replaces.

architect.resourceImport.unsupported.defaultMessage: That file type is not supported as a resource.
architect.resourceImport.unsupported.description: Error shown when the file added as a resource is not one of the file types Architect accepts.

architect.stageEditor.languages.descript.description: Description of the stage editor section listing the languages a participant can choose between. count is how many languages the protocol has. The Languages page is the page of the same name in the project navigation.

architect.stageEditor.languages.title.description: Heading of the stage editor section listing the languages a participant can choose between on a language chooser stage.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.com.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: everything it asks for has been filled in and nothing in it is invalid. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.err.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor (a stage is one step of an interview): something the researcher has entered in it is not valid. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen — the same state is drawn as a color and an icon.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.inc.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: it still has required fields the researcher has not filled in. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.lan.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark listing the sections of the stage being edited. A stage is one step of an interview.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.sta.description: Read out for a section of a stage editor whose only account of what is wrong is here. status is the section’s spoken state ("Has a problem"); problems is one or more whole sentences describing what the protocol refused, already in the reader’s language. Both are complete sentences, so this is only the punctuation that separates them.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.swi.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: the researcher has turned this optional part of the stage off, so it asks for nothing. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

architect.stageEditor.sectionOutline.una.description: Spoken state of one section of a stage editor: it cannot be filled in until something else in the stage has been chosen. Read out after the section’s own name, and never shown on screen.

architect.stageEditor.stageDraftConflict.description: Button in the dialog asking what to do with unsaved stage changes. Closes the dialog without choosing; nothing is changed or discarded.

Button in the dialog asking what to do with unsaved stage changes. Leaves the stage editor and throws away the unsaved changes to the stage, keeping the version the other tab saved. It cannot be undone.
Button in the dialog asking what to do with unsaved stage changes after the other tab closed. Downloads a copy of the protocol including the unsaved stage changes; the dialog then asks again.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.cannot.description: Title of the dialog shown when the protocol, with the stage being edited, is invalid and so cannot be previewed. The body shows the technical validation error.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.discar.description: Button in the confirmation dialog for leaving the stage editor; throws away the unsaved stage changes and returns to the timeline.
Title of the confirmation dialog shown when the researcher cancels or leaves the stage editor while the stage has unsaved changes.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.failed.description: Fallback body of the Preview Failed dialog, used when the error gives no more specific reason that could be shown instead.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.noProt.description: Body of the Preview Error dialog, shown when the preview was requested but there is no open protocol to preview.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.oK.description: Button that dismisses the Stage not found dialog.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.previe.description: Title of the error dialog shown when the Preview button is pressed but no protocol is loaded.
Title of the error dialog shown when opening the preview window failed unexpectedly.
Title of the dialog shown when the browser blocked the new window that the preview opens in.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.respec.description: Label of a toggle in the preview options menu of the stage editor toolbar. When on, the preview applies the protocol's skip logic and so may skip stages, as a real interview would.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.stageN.description: Title of the info dialog shown when the researcher opens the address of a timeline stage that no longer exists in the protocol.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.startP.description: Label of a toggle in the preview options menu of the stage editor toolbar. When on, the preview begins with generated example data (nodes and edges) instead of an empty network.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.thatSt.defaultMessage: That stage no longer exists. It may have been deleted. Returning you to the protocol overview.
architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.thatSt.description: Body of the info dialog shown when the stage the researcher tried to open no longer exists. Architect then returns to the protocol overview (the timeline).

architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.yourBr.defaultMessage: Your browser blocked the preview popup. Allow popups for this site, then click Preview again.
architect.stageEditor.stageEditor.yourBr.description: Body of the Preview popup blocked dialog. Tells the researcher to allow popups for this site and press the Preview button in the stage editor toolbar again.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditorChrome..description: Button that closes the dialog shown when the interview preview cannot start from the stage editor, either because no protocol is loaded or because the stage has errors.

architect.stageEditor.stageEditorPage.ot.description: What an editor calls the browser tab that holds the saved copy of this protocol, when it is not this one. Read as, for example, “Another tab is editing this stage”.

architect.stageEditor.stageTitle.documen.description: Link beside the name of the stage being edited, to the documentation for this type of interview interface.

architect.stageEditor.stageTitle.positio.description: Where the stage being edited sits in the interview, shown above its name. index is one-based. A stage is one step of an interview.

architect.storageUnavailableBanner.downl.description: Title of the error dialog shown when downloading the protocol from the storage-unavailable banner failed unexpectedly.
Button in the storage-unavailable banner. Downloads the protocol as a .netcanvas file so work is not lost. The extension .netcanvas is the file format name and stays as it is.

architect.storageUnavailableBanner.oK.description: Button that dismisses the dialogs shown after a failed attempt to download the protocol from the storage-unavailable banner.

architect.storageUnavailableBanner.someA.defaultMessage: Some resources could not be read
architect.storageUnavailableBanner.someA.description: Title of the dialog shown when downloading the protocol was stopped because some resources (uploaded files such as images, video or audio) could not be read.

architect.storageUnavailableBanner.thisP.defaultMessage: This protocol isn't being saved on this device — local app storage is unavailable, which is common in private browsing. Download a copy to keep your work.
architect.storageUnavailableBanner.thisP.description: Warning banner across the protocol editor, shown when the browser's local storage is unavailable (common in private browsing) so the open protocol is held only in memory. Its button downloads a copy.

architect.storageUnavailableBanner.yourP.defaultMessage: Your protocol couldn't be downloaded. Please try again.
architect.storageUnavailableBanner.yourP.description: Body of the Download failed dialog, shown when downloading the protocol failed unexpectedly. Asks the researcher to try again.

architect.submission.failed.defaultMessage: These changes could not be saved. Check the current settings and try again.
architect.submission.failed.description: Actionable fallback for an unexpected editor submission failure. Technical exception text is not shown as repair guidance.

architect.submission.missingAttribute.description: Submission failure when the selected attribute disappeared while the editor was open.

architect.submission.rowRemoved.defaultMessage: This item was removed while your changes were being saved, so there is nothing left to save them to. Copy anything you want to keep, then cancel and add a new item.
architect.submission.rowRemoved.description: A row disappeared during its asynchronous save. Whole neutral wording avoids capturing a previously translated item label.

architect.summary.prompt.ascending.description: Value in the sort order list of a prompt in the printable protocol summary, shown in brackets after a property: items are sorted from lowest to highest.

architect.summary.prompt.highlightattrib.description: Row label in a prompt's table in the printable protocol summary; its value is the variable set when a participant highlights a node.

architect.summary.prompt.layoutattribute.description: Row label in a prompt's table in the printable protocol summary; its value is the variable that stores the position of each node on the sociogram.

architect.summary.prompt.negativeOptionL.description: Row label in a prompt's table in the printable protocol summary; its value is the text of the answer button that means none of the options apply.

architect.summary.prompt.otherattribute.description: Row label in a prompt's table in the printable protocol summary; its value is the variable that stores the text a participant types for an "other" answer.

architect.summary.prompt.otheroptionlabe.description: Row label in a prompt's table in the printable protocol summary; its value is the text of the "other" answer option.

architect.summary.prompt.sortbyproperty.description: Row label in a prompt's table in the printable protocol summary; its value lists the properties used to sort the nodes shown to participants.

architect.summary.scaffolding.enabled.description: Yes or no value in the printable protocol summary of a family tree census stage, saying whether the quick start dialog is shown. enabled is true or false.

architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.howToG.defaultMessage: How to get a Mapbox token
architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.howToG.description: Button in the Mapbox token alerts. Opens Mapbox's help page, in a new browser tab, on how to create an access token.

architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.revoke.description: Title of an error alert at the top of the timeline, shown when the protocol uses Network Canvas's retired Mapbox testing token. Mapbox is the map service used by Geospatial stages.

architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.thisPr.defaultMessage: This protocol uses a retired Network Canvas Mapbox testing token. It was revoked on 2 September 2026, so maps in Geospatial stages will not load. Replace it with your own token in the Resource Library.
architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.thisPr.description: Body of the error alert about the revoked Mapbox testing token. Says maps in Geospatial stages will not load and tells the researcher to replace the token with their own in the Resource Library.

architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.thisPr.defaultMessage: This protocol uses Network Canvas's shared Mapbox testing token so the map renders out of the box. It is rate-limited and for evaluation only. Before you deploy this study, replace it with your own token in the Resource Library.
architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.thisPr.description: Body of the warning alert about the shared Mapbox testing token. Says it is rate-limited and for evaluation only, and tells the researcher to replace it with their own token in the Resource Library before deploying the study.

architect.testingMapboxTokenAlert.usingA.description: Title of a warning alert at the top of the timeline, shown when the protocol uses Network Canvas's shared Mapbox testing token.

architect.timeline.announcement.deleted.defaultMessage: Deleted stage {position, number}. {remaining, plural, =0 {No stages remain.} one {1 stage remains.} other {# stages remain.}}
architect.timeline.announcement.deleted.description: Live announcement after a timeline operation succeeds.

architect.timeline.announcement.moved.defaultMessage: Moved stage {fromPosition, number} to position {toPosition, number} of {total, number}.
architect.timeline.announcement.moved.description: Live announcement after a timeline operation succeeds.

architect.timeline.finishStageGuards.can.description: Title of the notice shown when a move would put a stage after a stage that ends the interview.

architect.timeline.finishStageGuards.fin.defaultMessage: You cannot delete this 'finish interview' stage because at least one stage of this kind is required to allow the interview to end.
architect.timeline.finishStageGuards.fin.description: Tooltip and accessible description of the unavailable delete button of the only stage that ends the interview (the finish screen), saying why it cannot be deleted.

architect.timeline.finishStageGuards.fin.defaultMessage: Stages that end the interview have to stay together at the end of the protocol. No participant could reach a stage placed after them.
architect.timeline.finishStageGuards.fin.description: Explanation shown when a researcher tries to move a stage that ends the interview above another kind of stage, or to move another kind of stage below one. Stages that end the interview can still change places with each other.

architect.timeline.insertButton.addStage.description: Visible label of the button between two stages on the timeline that adds a new stage at that point. It appears when the button is hovered or focused.

architect.timeline.insertButton.addStage.defaultMessage: Add stage here, before stage {position, number}: {nextStageName}
architect.timeline.insertButton.addStage.description: Accessible name of the button between two stages on the timeline that adds a new stage there; read only by screen readers. position is the number the new stage would take; nextStageName is the name of the stage it would be inserted before.

architect.timeline.timeline.addNewStage.description: Button at the end of the timeline. Opens the dialog for choosing the interface type of a new stage, which is added after the last stage.

architect.timeline.timeline.areYouSureYo.defaultMessage: Are you sure you want to delete this stage from your protocol? You can restore it with Undo while this protocol remains open.
architect.timeline.timeline.areYouSureYo.description: Body of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm deleting a stage from the timeline. Undo is the protocol editor's undo command.

architect.timeline.timeline.cannotDelete.description: Title of the dialog shown when the researcher tries to delete a Family Pedigree stage that a Narrative Pedigree stage still uses.

architect.timeline.timeline.deleteStage.description: Title of the dialog that asks the researcher to confirm deleting a stage from the timeline.

architect.timeline.timeline.oK.description: Button that dismisses the warning dialogs on the timeline, such as the ones for a stage that cannot be deleted.

architect.timeline.timeline.protocolStag.description: Accessible name of the list of stages on the timeline; read only by screen readers.

architect.timeline.timeline.thisFamilyPe.defaultMessage: {stageCount, plural, one {This Family Pedigree stage is used by the Narrative Pedigree stage {names}. Remove that stage or change its source before deleting this stage.} other {This Family Pedigree stage is used by the Narrative Pedigree stages {names}. Remove those stages or change their source before deleting this stage.}}
architect.timeline.timeline.thisFamilyPe.description: Body of the Cannot delete stage dialog. stageCount is the number of Narrative Pedigree stages that use this Family Pedigree stage as their source; names is the list of those stages.

architect.timeline.timelineStageRow.dele.description: Accessible name of the trash button on a timeline stage that deletes the stage, after confirmation. position is its number in the timeline; stageName is its title.

architect.timeline.timelineStageRow.hasF.description: Alternative text and tooltip of a small icon on a timeline stage, shown when the stage has a filter set.

architect.timeline.timelineStageRow.hasS.description: Alternative text and tooltip of a small icon on a timeline stage, shown when the stage has skip logic set.

architect.typeEditor.shapePicker.config..description: Name of the circle node shape, shown under its swatch in the shape picker of the node type editor.
Name of the diamond node shape, shown under its swatch in the shape picker of the node type editor.
Name of the square node shape, shown under its swatch in the shape picker of the node type editor.

architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.description: Label of the dropdown in the node type editor's shape mapping that chooses which variable of the node type decides the node's shape. Attribute means a codebook variable.
Label of the fixed first row in the thresholds list of the shape mapping. It covers values lower than the lowest threshold, which use the default shape.

architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.defaultMessage: Below first threshold cannot be removed
architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.description: Accessible name of the disabled delete button in the fixed Below first threshold row; read only by screen readers. The row always exists and cannot be removed.
Accessible name of the disabled shape picker in the fixed Below first threshold row; it shows the node type's default shape. Read only by screen readers.
Label of the False value of a yes/no variable in the shape mapping of the node type editor, beside the picker for the shape used when the variable is false.
Label and accessible name of the on/off toggle in the node type editor that lets a variable of the node type decide the node shape instead of one default shape.

architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.defaultMessage: Override the default shape based on the value of a node's attribute.
architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.description: Hint below the Map attribute to shape toggle. Attribute means a variable recorded about each node of this type.
Accessible remove-button label for a shape-mapping threshold. value1 is its one-based position in the threshold list.
Accessible label for the shape chosen at a numeric breakpoint. value is the complete locale-formatted threshold number; its precision must be preserved.
Accessible name of the shape picker beside one value of the variable in the shape mapping; read only by screen readers. value1 is the value's label.
Heading above the list of a categorical, ordinal or yes/no variable's values in the shape mapping, each with a picker for the shape used for that value.
Hidden field label (accessible name only) of the shape mapping editor, which holds the chosen variable and its value-to-shape rules.

architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.defaultMessage: Some values are unmapped and will use the default shape.
architect.typeEditor.shapeVariableMappin.description: Warning below the list of values in the shape mapping, shown while at least one value has no shape chosen. Those nodes use the node type's default shape.
Accessible name of a numeric shape-mapping threshold input. value1 is the one-based threshold position, not the numeric breakpoint value.
Heading and accessible name of the list of numeric thresholds in the shape mapping for a number or scale variable. Each threshold is a value at or above which nodes use a chosen shape.
Label of the True value of a yes/no variable in the shape mapping of the node type editor, beside the picker for the shape used when the variable is true.
Small note at the end of the fixed Below first threshold row, saying that values below the first threshold use the node type's default shape.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.chooseAC.description: Hint under the colour picker in the type editor. entity is node, edge or ego, the kind of type being edited.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.chooseAD.defaultMessage: Choose a default shape and optionally map shapes from an attribute.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.interfac.description: Heading of the section of the node type editor where an icon is chosen for the interface stages that create nodes of this type.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.nameThis.defaultMessage: Name this type for the codebook and exported data.
architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.nameThis.description: Description under the Type identity section heading in the node or edge type editor.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.nodeAppe.description: Heading of the section of the node type editor that sets how nodes of this type look (their shape).

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.shape.description: Label of the default node shape picker in the node type editor.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.typeColo.description: Heading of the section of the node or edge type editor where the type's colour is chosen.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.typeIden.description: Heading of the first section of the node or edge type editor, containing the type's name.

architect.typeEditor.typeEditor.typeName.description: Label of the name field in the type editor. entity is node or edge, depending on which kind of type is being edited.
